title: Exodus Bible Quiz - Chapter 38
description: Ten questions on Exodus 38: the bronze altar and basin, the court of the tabernacle and the metals given for the work.

questions.text: What was the length of the altar of burnt offering?
questions.explanation: He made the altar of burnt offering of acacia wood. It was square: five cubits long, five cubits wide and three cubits high.

questions.text: With what metal did he overlay the altar of burnt offering?
questions.explanation: He made its horns of one piece with it, and he overlaid it with bronze.

questions.text: Out of what was the bronze basin and its base made?
questions.explanation: He made the basin of bronze, and its base of bronze, out of the mirrors of the ministering women who ministered at the door of the Tent of Meeting.

answers.text: The bronze shields of the soldiers
The cooking pots of the Levites
The mirrors of the ministering women
The bronze bells of the rulers

questions.text: How long were the hangings of the court on the south side?
questions.explanation: For the south side the hangings of the court were of fine twined linen, one hundred cubits.

questions.text: What were the hooks of the court's pillars and their fillets made of?
questions.explanation: The sockets for the pillars were of bronze, but the hooks of the pillars and their fillets were of silver.

questions.text: What was the length of the screen for the gate of the court?
questions.explanation: The screen for the gate of the court was embroidered work; twenty cubits was the length, and the height five cubits.

questions.text: By whose hand were the materials for the tabernacle counted?
questions.explanation: The materials were counted according to the commandment of Moses, for the service of the Levites, by the hand of Ithamar, the son of Aaron the priest.

answers.text: Eleazar, the son of Aaron the priest

questions.text: How is Oholiab described in this chapter?
questions.explanation: Oholiab of the tribe of Dan was an engraver, a skillful workman and an embroiderer in blue, purple, scarlet and fine linen.

answers.text: A priest who served at the altar
A ruler of Israel who brought the onyx stones
An engraver, a skillful workman and an embroiderer
A shepherd who brought the rams' skins

questions.text: How much silver did each counted man give?
questions.explanation: Each man counted from twenty years old and upward gave a beka a head, that is, half a shekel, according to the shekel of the sanctuary.

answers.text: A beka, that is, half a shekel
One talent of silver per man

questions.text: What was made with the bronze of the offering?
questions.explanation: With the bronze he made the sockets to the door of the Tent of Meeting, the bronze altar, its bronze grating, all the vessels of the altar, the sockets of the court and all the pins.

answers.text: The lamp stand with its seven lamps
The bronze altar and its grating
The mercy seat and its cherubim
